name: OPA827 (single low-noise precision JFET-input)
tagline: TI's 2006 single JFET op-amp (4 nV/√Hz, 22 MHz) that DIYers treat as the modern OPA627: a DAC I/V favourite, called 'successor to the legendary stone' in a Japanese review.
technology: JFET-input precision voltage-feedback op-amp. Supply ±4 V to ±18 V (8 to 36 V total), abs max 40 V. Specified from -40 °C to +125 °C. Packages: SOIC-8 (D) and VSSOP/MSOP-8 (DGK). Input common-mode range and output swing are not rail-to-rail: both reach only to within 3 V of each rail. Only the single ever reached production. Early SBOS376 revisions (2006 to 2008) were titled 'OPA827, OPA2827' and announced a dual OPA2827 as Product Preview. That is why the datasheet says 'OPA827 series' and carried 'Mixed Status'. The 2013 orderables list has no OPA2827, and no evidence was found that it ever shipped. Before Rev G (Feb 2012) the datasheet also listed a high grade, OPA827I. TI's later dual in this line is OPA2828, in production since Dec 2022.

Datasheet SBOS376: original Nov 2006, Rev C Aug 2007, Rev E Sep 2008, Rev F Mar 2009, Rev G Feb 2012, Rev H May 2012, Rev I Jul 2016 (still current in 2026). Several mirrors label early copies 'Burr-Brown', which suggests BB-branded early datasheets (unconfirmed). No second source.

TI's OPAx828 datasheet (SBOS671D, Sep 2018, revised Dec 2022) calls OPA828/OPA2828 'the next generation OPA627 and OPA827' (from a local extract; not re-searched this run). 45 MHz GBW, 150 V/us, 4 nV/√Hz. OPA2828 comes in DGN only.

reputation.summary: Hi-Fi DIYers treat it as the cheaper modern successor to the OPA627. They use it mostly as a DAC I/V converter and in socket-rolled line and headphone stages on SOIC-to-DIP adapters. In Xonar Essence ST/STX I/V discussions it is named with LT1361, LT1028 and OPA627 as the best I/V choices. Impressions conflict. English-forum posts gathered by an earlier sweep (not re-read) call it almost neutral, clean and more dynamic and less fickle than the OPA627. A diyAudio 'Best Sounding DUAL opamps' thread describes it as bass-centric, dark, warm and laid-back, with an impressive soundstage. In Japan two Zigsow reviews carry the titles 'The strongest lineage' and 'Successor to the legendary stone', the stone being the OPA627. TI's datasheet supports audio use (-128 dB THD+N at 3 Vrms/600 Ω; 'professional audio applications'). No ASR or Samuel Groner measurement was found.
sonic_descriptors: very clean, clear and fluid (lens note)
more dynamic and less fickle than OPA627 (lens note)
bass-centric; deep, dark, warm, laid-back (diyAudio dual-opamps thread)
more assertive low end than OPA2111 (one Japanese swap report)
typical_uses: DAC current-to-voltage (I/V) stage, e.g. socket rolling in Asus Xonar Essence ST/STX I/V positions
Portable DAC/headphone-amp op-amp swaps on DIP-8 adapters (e.g. a 2015 Fostex HP-A4 OPA827 swap blog)
Engineering (datasheet application list): 16- to 18-bit ADC drivers, DAC output buffers, transimpedance amps, filters, precision ±10 V front ends, professional audio
caveats: SMD only (SOIC-8 / VSSOP-8), so socket use needs a DIP-8 adapter. It is single channel, so a dual socket needs two parts on a 2-in-1 adapter.
Not rail-to-rail: input CM range and output swing reach only to within 3 V of each rail. On ±5 V rails usable swing is only about ±2 V.
4.8 mA typ (5.2 mA max) quiescent current per channel, and it needs at least ±4 V (8 V total).
22 MHz GBW on adapter boards: keep supply decoupling at the chip (general practice, not a documented failure report).
Listener impressions conflict (neutral/clean vs dark/warm/bass-centric). Several descriptors come from lens summaries, not first-hand re-reads.
DC precision: a PhD thesis (PatrickBaus) saw non-symmetric cubic INL with OPA827 as an ADC buffer, and a 2019 blog shows higher 1/f noise than the OPA227 near DC.
JFET bias current rises steeply with temperature (±5 nA max at 125 °C vs ±10 pA at 25 °C).
Costs much more than common audio duals.
sources: https://zigsow.jp/item/261371/review/319336%20(title:%20伝説の石の後継品%20-%20OPA827AIDのレビュー)

silicon_changes.summary: TI PCN#20240628012.1, 'Qualification alternate Mount & Mold Compound material for select devices', lists OPA827AID among several op-amp and reference devices. It qualifies an alternate die-attach (mount) and mold-compound material set. No die, fab or datasheet change is involved; the datasheet was not revised afterwards.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Negligible. Mount and mold-compound changes have no datasheet-level electrical effect. Mold stress can shift precision offset slightly, but no such effect is documented.

silicon_changes.summary: At Rev G the datasheet moved from Mixed Status to Production Data. TI changed the input bias current and input offset drift Features bullets and the drift/bias text in the Description, and deleted the planned high-grade option (and its footnote) from the ordering table. Offset, drift and bias limits were set, and SR and short-circuit current minimums were added. This was a datasheet change, most likely final characterisation. No PCN or die change was found, so it is a spec hazard, not a confirmed silicon change.

counterfeit_notes: No OPA827-specific counterfeit or remarking report surfaced, but no search this run targeted counterfeits. Genuine TI markings per the SBOS376H package addendum (Oct 2013): SOIC-8 (D) reads 'OPA / 827 / A' plus logo and lot/date code; VSSOP-8 (DGK) reads 'NSP'. DGK lead finish may be NiPdAu or NiPdAuAg. TI has only ever listed the D and DGK packages, so a DIP-8 'OPA827' is not a genuine TI package. The OPA2827 dual never went beyond Product Preview, so any 'OPA2827' offered for sale is suspect. The part is often sold pre-soldered on adapters by marketplace sellers, and its benchmark OPA627 is among the most-faked audio op-amps. Buy from TI or authorised distributors, and check Iq (4.8 mA typ) and slew rate (at least 20 V/us).

revision_chain_notes: TI SBOS376 (OPA827; OPA2827 in the preview editions). Chain, oldest to newest: original, Nov 2006 (Product Preview, OPA827/OPA2827) -> A, Nov 2006 original date, revised date not shown (preview specs: 250 uV max offset, 18 MHz, 22 V/us) -> B, date unknown, still no evidence it exists -> C, Aug 2007 (a summary shows the header 'SBOS376C-NOVEMBER 2006-REVISED AUGUST 2007' and ties it to a PRODUCT PREVIEW OPA827/OPA2827 edition, probably the listed Octopart datasheet-153423) -> D, date unknown (an exact search for "SBOS376D" returned nothing) -> E, Sep 2008 (Octopart 5394927) -> F, Mar 2009 -> G, Feb 2012 (Octopart 10745194 contains the F-to-G change list, so it is G or later) -> H, May 2012 -> I, Jul 2016 (current). Still missing: a copy of B and its date, a copy of D and its date, the revised date of A, the H-to-I change list, and a copy firmly tied to F (a search for 'REVISED MARCH 2009' found nothing). New unverified copies worth reading: datasheetspdf 562972 (OPA2827, maybe Rev A), alldatasheet 195278 (BB, probably preview), ic37 5676975 (BB), alldatasheet 849336 (TI1) and Mouser opa827-406900.pdf. The archive seeds are built from the standard focus.ti.com / ti.com symlink and product-folder URL patterns and have not been checked. No other vendor or second source has ever made the OPA827. Searches used: 6 of 6.
